model_note.S:
cc: Pain migrating to the right lower abdomen

HPI: 27 yo f. Patient reports: The pain began 18 hours ago. It is now in the right lower abdomen. It moved from around my belly button to the right lower side. It is a steady sharp ache. It is 7/10. It has steadily worsened. It began before I vomited; there was no injury. Lying still with my knees bent helps a little. Walking, coughing and bumps in the car worsen it. I took acetaminophen without much relief. This has never happened before. I have no appetite. I feel nauseated. I vomited once after the pain began. I have felt feverish since this morning.

Patient perspective: I assumed it was food poisoning; could I just go home?

PMH: No chronic illnesses.

PSH: No abdominal surgery or hospitalizations.

Meds: Acetaminophen 500 mg once; no daily medication.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One alcoholic drink weekly. No recreational drugs. Graduate student; lives with my husband; sexually active, condoms usually; last menstrual period 5 weeks ago, pregnancy possible.

FH: Mother has hypertension; father and sister are healthy.

ROS: Gastrointestinal - Reports anorexia. Reports nausea. Reports vomiting. General - Reports fever. Denies chills. Denies weight loss. Urinary - Denies dysuria. Denies hematuria. Denies frequency.
Pain pattern: The pain is constant.
Bowel history: My bowel movements have been usual. I have not had diarrhea or constipation.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 100.6 F oral, P 106 bpm, BP 116/72 mmHg, R 18 rpm, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Uncomfortable, remaining still on the examination table.

Heart: Regular tachycardia without murmur.

Lungs: Breath sounds clear bilaterally.

Abd: Abdomen not distended; no surgical scars. Bowel sounds present. Focal right lower quadrant tenderness. Involuntary guarding in the right lower quadrant. Tenderness at McBurney point. Tympany over the examined quadrants.

Osteopathic: T5 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Transfer to the emergency department immediately for surgical evaluation; obtain pregnancy testing, CBC, BMP, urinalysis and pregnancy-appropriate abdominal imaging; provide clinician-directed analgesia and fluids; explain concern for an acute abdominal process and use emergency disposition now.

2. Urgently obtain pregnancy test and pelvic ultrasound when indicated; involve obstetrics/gynecology for suspected ectopic pregnancy and monitor circulation; explain that pregnancy-related emergencies must be excluded despite uncertain pregnancy status.

3. Obtain urinalysis and pregnancy-appropriate renal imaging if the pattern suggests a stone; assess obstruction and infection, provide appropriate analgesia, and obtain urgent urology input for infected obstruction.

model_note.S:
cc: Pain migrating to the right lower abdomen

HPI: 27 yo f. Patient reports: The pain began 10 hours ago. It is now in the right lower abdomen. It moved from around my belly button to the right lower side. It is a steady sharp ache. It is 7/10. It has steadily worsened. It began before I vomited; there was no injury. Lying still with my knees bent helps a little. Walking, coughing and bumps in the car worsen it. I took acetaminophen without much relief. This has never happened before. I have no appetite. I feel nauseated. I vomited once after the pain began. I have felt feverish since this morning.

Patient perspective: I assumed it was food poisoning; could I just go home?

PMH: No chronic illnesses.

PSH: No abdominal surgery or hospitalizations.

Meds: Acetaminophen 500 mg once; no daily medication.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. One alcoholic drink weekly. No recreational drugs. Graduate student; lives with my husband; sexually active, condoms usually; last menstrual period 5 weeks ago, pregnancy possible.

FH: Mother has hypertension; father and sister are healthy.

ROS: Gastrointestinal - Reports anorexia. Reports nausea. Reports vomiting. General - Reports fever. Denies chills. Denies weight loss. Urinary - Denies dysuria. Denies hematuria. Denies frequency.
Pain pattern: The pain is constant.
Bowel history: My bowel movements have been usual. I have not had diarrhea or constipation.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 100.6 F oral, P 106 bpm, BP 116/72 mmHg, R 18 rpm, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 7", Wt 165 lbs

General: Alert. Uncomfortable, remaining still on the examination table.

Heart: Regular tachycardia without murmur.

Lungs: Breath sounds clear bilaterally.

Abd: Abdomen not distended; no surgical scars. Bowel sounds present. Focal right lower quadrant tenderness. Involuntary guarding in the right lower quadrant. Tenderness at McBurney point. Tympany over the examined quadrants.

Osteopathic: T5 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.

Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Transfer to the emergency department immediately for surgical evaluation; obtain pregnancy testing, CBC, BMP, urinalysis and pregnancy-appropriate abdominal imaging; provide clinician-directed analgesia and fluids; explain concern for an acute abdominal process and use emergency disposition now.

2. Urgently obtain pregnancy test and pelvic ultrasound when indicated; involve obstetrics/gynecology for suspected ectopic pregnancy and monitor circulation; explain that pregnancy-related emergencies must be excluded despite uncertain pregnancy status.

3. Obtain urinalysis and pregnancy-appropriate renal imaging if the pattern suggests a stone; assess obstruction and infection, provide appropriate analgesia, and obtain urgent urology input for infected obstruction.
